Q: Why when I create object, the variable contains a reference to the object, not the object it self? A:

"Why when I create object, the variable contains a reference to the object, not the object it self?"

Yea, variable = reference. And (NOT object) object instance in heap mem, and for example methods for this object (methods for this type) where? How you explain object? Object is a big big think, see here at start: If a beginner asks you about the object, how do you explain it?

You have CPU and mem, please explain how you destroy formal all [variable = reference], and use only object instance? Link above used BMP-object, see link. BUT! BMP-object is not a language! Im understand your idea, total destroy references and total using objects. And this very right idea, but object instances in memory must be aligned, and some indicies must be for offsets to all object instances in memory. Then your idea completely works, BUT! For tiny sub-set of all object instances.

P.s.: Forget all languages, all you have is CPU and mem. And simplest actions with that.

Formal system here:

[in-memory]
{ SelfMetadataBytes0, SelfMetadataBytes1, ... UserDataBytes0, UserDataBytes1, ... }

Okay, object instances without metadata, how? In Dot.NET terminology like this:

public struct Struct { public field0; public field1; }
public Struct[] Structs = new Struct[];

[in-memory]
{ UserDataBytes0, UserDataBytes1, ... UserDataBytesN, UserDataBytesN+1, ... }

Here your object instances without references (payload only). But need offsets!

P.p.s: What you want is already invented and exists. In Dot.NET terminology, it's array of structures. There's one reference for everything, and accessing structures is NOT OVERWRITING reference variable (CPU register), it's shifting reference. This is crucial because overwriting reference variable is expensive, while shifting without changing reference (shifting = offsetting) is very cheap. You need look code in assembly for these operations, but generally all this covered in first year of your local university. This is how it should be.

Q: Windows Terminal - open new tab with current environment A:

I came here with this same question, and was surprised to find there weren't any answers. I wonder if wt has been changed/improved since this was asked as I eventually found the following works:

wt -w 0 nt --inheritEnvironment

This starts a new tab in the current terminal session, with the same environment as the tab it is run in.

Note that the capital E is necessary.

Q: How to pass String url into URL of kotlin? A:

import io.ktor.http.Url

Q: Colab RAM is Almost Full After Training Although I Delete The Variables A:

I hope that someone can post a better answer. Sharing so my account gets a notification if someone else has a fix

This is how I handle the issue:

  1. Use #@param annotations to create input widgets which cache the high memory operation
  2. The first time it runs, check the input widget to regenerate the data
  3. After generating the data, uncheck the input widget to load the results from GDrive

Colab Python:

import pickle
from google.colab import drive
drive.mount(r'/content/gdrive/')
CACHE_DIR = "/content/gdrive/MyDrive/CACHE_DIR/"

regenerate_HIGH_MEM_models = True #@param{type:"boolean"}
HIGH_MEM_models_file = "HIGH_MEM_models_2022.pkl"  #@param {type:"string"}

if regenerate_HIGH_MEM_models:
  HIGH_MEM_models = generate_models_HIGH_MEM()
  with open(f"{CACHE_DIR}{ranked_universe_models_file}", "wb") as file: 
      pickle.dump(HIGH_MEM_models, file)
else:
  #@markdown (will load file from Gdrive if not regenerating)
  with open(f"{CACHE_DIR}{HIGH_MEM_models_file}", "rb") as file: 
      HIGH_MEM_models = pickle.load(file)

Q: "FirefoxDriver cannot be resolved to a type" when running Selenium webdriver A:

Try adding selenium stand alone server(https://docs.seleniumhq.org/download/) to your project (even though you are using maven), as an external jar and try. For me this resolution worked. Right click on your Maven project > Properties > Java Buildpath > Libraries tab Click on Add External jar button > Browse to the folder where the jar is saved > upload >Apply and close
